# Wafly HTTP starter

## Who is this for?
Integrators who want a small, manual first-message test with the Wafly REST API using native n8n nodes, without installing a community node or connecting an AI account.

## How it works
Edit Fields holds your configuration. A Code node validates one input and requires explicit recipient authorization. HTTP Request sends one text message and is disabled by default. There is no schedule, contact list, loop, or automatic retry.

## Setup
1. Create your own [Wafly account](https://wafly.com.br/signup?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=workflow_template&utm_campaign=wafly_http_starter_202610&utm_content=creator_description) and connect an instance you control.
2. Replace the placeholders. Use your own or an explicitly authorized recipient and set `authorizedRecipient` to true only after checking it.
3. Create a Header Auth credential: name `Client-Token`, value your private client token. Select it in HTTP Request.
4. Enable HTTP Request only when ready, then run the manual trigger once.

The instance token is part of the API URL and private workflow configuration. Restrict project access and remove tokens before sharing exports or screenshots. A timeout may occur after acceptance: verify before repeating. HTTP 2xx/messageId is acceptance, not delivery or reading; check your own device.

## Requirements and disclosure
Wafly is a paid, managed, non-official WhatsApp API with a three-day trial; regional pricing applies. It is not Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API, and account restriction risks remain. No unsolicited bulk messaging. Maintained by the Wafly team. [Setup guide](https://wafly.com.br/tutoriais/enviar-mensagem-whatsapp-api/).

## Configure privately
Replace the placeholders in Edit Fields. Use your own connected instance and an authorized recipient. Set authorizedRecipient to true only after checking the number.

In HTTP Request, select your Header Auth credential: Client-Token = your client token. Instance tokens are sensitive URL components: never share a configured export.

## One deliberate attempt
HTTP Request is disabled until you finish setup. Enable it, then run the manual trigger once. Automatic retries are off.

2xx/messageId means API acceptance, not WhatsApp delivery or reading. A timeout can happen after acceptance: check your own device before repeating. This is not a bulk messaging workflow.
